summary: A surviving spouse is guaranteed one half of the estate, or one third if there are children, and children can ask a court for proper provision. Ireland is an EU state outside the Succession Regulation. Trusts are recognised, though Ireland is not in the Hague Trusts Convention.
reserved_share: Spouse or civil partner: 1/2 of the estate (no children) or 1/3 (with children); Succession Act 1965 s. 111. Children have no fixed share but may claim under s. 117.
foreign_law_note: Ireland opted out of Regulation 650/2012. Irish rules apply domicile law to movables and the law of location to immovables; there is no nationality choice.
trust_note: Common-law trusts apply but Ireland has not joined the Hague Trusts Convention. Discretionary trusts pay capital acquisitions tax: 6% on creation plus 1% a year. The Irish foundation company is a guarantee company, with no separate foundation statute.
open_questions: Current CAT discretionary trust rates were not rechecked.
Whether any statutory private foundation was added.
